Quotations 121–144 of 673.

  1. The essential achievement of the will is to attend to a difficult object and hold it fast before the mind.
    William James
    Will
  2. Next to worry, probably one of the most potent causes of unhappiness is envy.
    Bertrand Russell
    Philosophy
  3. Envy is itself a terrible obstacle to happiness.
    Bertrand Russell
    Philosophy
  4. Fear is the main source of superstition, and one of the main sources of cruelty. To conquer fear is the beginning of wisdom.
    Bertrand Russell
    Fear
  5. The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
    Ludwig Wittgenstein
    Language
  6. We feel that even if all possible scientific questions are answered, the problems of life have still not been touched at all.
    Ludwig Wittgenstein
    Science
  7. The meaning of a word is its use in the language.
    Ludwig Wittgenstein
    Language
  8. In choosing himself, man chooses all men.
    Jean-Paul Sartre
    Choice
  9. Man is nothing other than what he makes of himself.
    Jean-Paul Sartre
    Self
  10. Rebellion cannot do without the notion of a limit — it stops at human dignity.
    Albert Camus
    Philosophy
  11. We may become the makers of our fate when we have ceased to pose as its prophets.
    Karl Popper
    Fate
  12. In the bitterest turns of fortune, true friends are proved.
    Boethius
    Friendship
  13. Wealth does not take away need — it kindles new wants.
    Boethius
    Wealth
  14. The Master said: Is it not a pleasure to learn and to practice what one has learned in due time? Is it not a joy to have friends come from afar? Is it not the mark of a gentleman to remain unresentful when others fail to appreciate one?
    Confucius
    Learning
  15. The Master said: What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others.
    Confucius
    Benevolence
  16. The Master said: You, shall I teach you what knowing is? To know what you know, and to know what you do not know — that is true knowing.
    Confucius
    Knowledge
  17. The Master said: When three people walk together, one of them is sure to be my teacher. I select what is good in them and follow it; what is not good, I correct in myself.
    Confucius
    Learning
  18. Zengzi said: Each day I examine myself on three counts: In acting on behalf of others, have I been loyal? In dealings with friends, have I been trustworthy? Have I practiced what was passed on to me?
    Zengzi
    Self-examination
  19. The Master said: When you see the worthy, think of equaling them; when you see the unworthy, examine yourself within.
    Confucius
    Self-examination
  20. The Master said: If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die content that evening.
    Confucius
    Way
  21. The Master said: The gentleman seeks it in himself; the petty person seeks it in others.
    Confucius
    Responsibility
  22. The Master said: When you have faults, do not fear to correct them.
    Confucius
    Philosophy
  23. The Master said: Only when the year turns cold do we know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither.
    Confucius
    Philosophy
  24. The Master said: Those who know it are not equal to those who love it; those who love it are not equal to those who delight in it.
    Confucius
    Learning
